newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mobutu entourage preparing for return to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu entourage preparing for return to Zaire.

text.p: The entourage of Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko began furious preparations on Friday for the ailing leader's return home after cancer treatment abroad.
Mobutu aides refused to talk to reporters outside the sprawling Riviera villa where the African leader has been recuperating from surgery for prostate cancer.
But Reuters correspondent Jean-Francois Roubaud said it appeared from the rush that he might leave as early as Saturday or Sunday.
"They are gathering baggage from aides who have been lodging in various hotels in the area, packing boxes and arranging things as if his departure were imminent," Roubaud said.
After several false alerts in November, associates and aides said earlier this week Mobutu would be heading home at the beginning of next week.
Mobutu arrived at the villa in southern France on November 4 after more than two months' treatment for his cancer in Lausanne, Switzerland.

In his absence, rebel troops have taken control of a swathe of territory about 500 km (300 miles) long in eastern Zaire, displacing hundreds of thousands of refugees from neighbouring Rwanda and Burundi, many of whom have since returned home.
The two-month offensive has seen the rebel coalition overwhelm Zaire's ragged army in the east, often without a fight, taking several key towns including Goma, Bukavu and Uvira.
Despite his apparent intention to return soon to Africa, Mobutu remains very weak, eyewitnesses said. Neighbours who saw him on Friday told Reuters he appeared very tired and ill.

Some Western leaders concerned over the vacuum of power in Zaire have said that only Mobutu has the power to keep his country together though he is persona non grata in many states because of his resistance to democracy, corruption allegations and criticisms of his human rights record.

"It is quite obvious that the international community cannot ignore that he is the man best placed to represent Zaire and find a solution to this problem as far as Zaire is concerned," French President Jacques Chirac said last month.

Laurent Kabila, political leader of the Tutsi-led rebels in eastern Zaire, declared a unilateral ceasefire on Thursday and urged the international community to push Zaire's government into negotiations.
He told Reuters that as part of the ceasefire the advancing rebels had stopped short of the towns of Walikale, west of Goma, and Bunia, north of Goma on the Ugandan border.
But Interior Minister Kamanda wa Kamanda told Reuters that Zaire saw neighbouring Rwanda as the aggressor in the east and Kinshasa would continue to do all in its power to recover its lost territory.
